subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What flame colour is produced by lithium ions in a flame test?
questions.explain: Lithium ions produce a characteristic crimson (red) flame.

questions.q: What flame colour is produced by sodium ions?
questions.explain: Sodium ions give a strong yellow flame colour.

questions.q: What flame colour is produced by potassium ions?
questions.explain: Potassium ions produce a lilac (light purple) flame.

questions.q: A solid gives a brick-red (orange-red) flame colour. Which metal ion is present?
questions.explain: Calcium ions produce a brick-red (orange-red) flame.

questions.q: An unknown salt burns with a lilac flame. Which ion does it contain?
questions.explain: A lilac flame indicates the presence of potassium ions.

questions.q: Which reagent is added to a solution to test for the presence of metal cations by forming coloured precipitates?
questions.explain: Adding sodium hydroxide solution forms metal hydroxide precipitates whose colours identify the cation.

questions.q: What colour precipitate forms when sodium hydroxide is added to a solution containing copper(II) ions?
questions.explain: Copper(II) ions form a blue precipitate of copper(II) hydroxide.

questions.q: What colour precipitate forms when sodium hydroxide is added to a solution containing iron(II) ions?
questions.explain: Iron(II) ions form a green precipitate of iron(II) hydroxide.

questions.q: A solution forms an orange-brown precipitate with sodium hydroxide. Which ion is present?
questions.explain: Iron(III) ions give an orange-brown precipitate of iron(III) hydroxide.

questions.q: A white precipitate forms when sodium hydroxide is added, and it redissolves when excess sodium hydroxide is added. Which cation is present?
questions.explain: Aluminium hydroxide is a white precipitate that dissolves in excess sodium hydroxide, unlike calcium hydroxide.

questions.q: How is the ammonium ion detected in a solution?
options: Warm with sodium hydroxide; ammonia gas turns damp red litmus paper blue
Add silver nitrate; a white precipitate forms
Add barium chloride; a white precipitate forms
Add dilute acid; effervescence turns limewater milky
questions.explain: Warming an ammonium salt with sodium hydroxide releases ammonia gas, which turns damp red litmus paper blue.

questions.q: Adding dilute acid to a solid produces bubbles of a gas that turns limewater milky. Which anion does the solid contain?
questions.explain: Carbonates react with dilute acid to release carbon dioxide, which turns limewater milky.

questions.q: Which procedure tests for the presence of sulfate ions?
options: Add dilute hydrochloric acid, then barium chloride solution; a white precipitate forms
Add dilute nitric acid, then silver nitrate solution; a white precipitate forms
Add sodium hydroxide solution; a blue precipitate forms
Add dilute acid; a gas that turns limewater milky is released
questions.explain: Sulfate ions give a white precipitate of barium sulfate with acidified barium chloride solution.

questions.q: When acidified silver nitrate is added to a solution containing chloride ions, what is observed?
questions.explain: Chloride ions form a white precipitate of silver chloride with acidified silver nitrate.

questions.q: A solution gives a cream precipitate when acidified silver nitrate is added. Which halide ion is present?
questions.explain: Bromide ions form a cream-coloured precipitate of silver bromide.

questions.q: A student adds dilute nitric acid then silver nitrate to a solution and sees a yellow precipitate. Which ion is present?
questions.explain: Iodide ions form a yellow precipitate of silver iodide with acidified silver nitrate.

questions.q: How is oxygen gas identified?
options: It produces a squeaky pop with a lighted splint
questions.explain: Oxygen relights a glowing splint.

questions.q: A lighted splint is held at the mouth of a test tube and a squeaky pop is heard. Which gas is present?
questions.explain: Hydrogen burns with a squeaky pop when a lighted splint is applied.

questions.q: A colourless gas turns limewater from clear to milky. Which gas is it?
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide turns limewater milky (cloudy) due to the formation of calcium carbonate.

questions.q: Which gas turns damp blue litmus paper red and then bleaches it white?
questions.explain: Chlorine bleaches damp litmus paper, turning it white.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Chemistry (2017) specification; Tests for Ions & Gases
